battle.name: 黃巢轉戰中原之戰
battle.brief: 乾符四年（877）起，黃巢放棄廣州根基，率眾自嶺南北還，取杭州、越州、潤州，渡江沿運河與淮水北上，連下亳、泗、楚諸州，進逼汴洛。叛軍以朴刀、長矛與弓弩混編，並備雲梯撞車攻城；卡面這柄外彎單刃的埃及月牙劍，正是「砍下不用拔」的早期砍劈刃原型，與唐代直刃環首刀恰成對照。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是唐王朝及其方鎮藩鎮，一方是黃巢自領的叛軍。唐方是典型的中晚唐結構：中央有左右神策軍、左右羽林軍等禁軍，但乾符年間禁軍已大為空虛，僖宗真正能直接調動的只有行在所置的護駕中軍與少數募兵；兵權與財權握在數十位節度使手中，節度使自置官吏、自徵賦稅、自募部曲。此次投入追討黃巢的，多為兗海節度使秦彥所部、河南道各鎮、忠武軍與武寧軍、淮南道、浙西道、嶺南道地方軍，以及奉詔西上的河東與關中兵馬，但彼此互不隸屬，奉詔則集兵，詔至則各歸本鎮，彼此之間的協同全靠詔書與宦官監軍勉強維繫。叛軍方面，黃巢自領的兵眾被朝廷詔書稱為「草寇」，旗號用黃，自號「衝天香陣」；877年攻陷廣州之後，他放棄嶺南的稅源與人煙，率眾東出北還，實際上是一支以私鹽販與失業農民為主、附有數萬騎兵的流動大軍。叛軍內部有幕僚核心：尚讓為謀主，葛從周、張希烈等為大將，分營分隊作戰，糧秣就地取給，不建營壘、不設器械廠，遇到城池能攻則攻、不能攻則繞行而過。僖宗出奔劍南之後，行在所設護駕中軍拱衛天子，東路各鎮仍各自為戰，雙方在指揮層面上其實並不對稱：一方是四面出兵的鬆散聯邦，一方是意志統一而裝備落後的流動軍。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the Tang dynasty with its regional military governors on one side, and the rebel army led by Huang Chao on the other. The Tang side shows the classic structure of the middle and late Tang: at the centre stood the imperial guards, the Left and Right Shence Army and the Left and Right Yulin Army, but by the Qianfu era these had been hollowed out, and the troops Xizong could actually move on his own authority were the escorting central army attached to the imperial party and a handful of recruits. Military power and revenue lay in the hands of several dozen jiedushi, who appointed their own officials, levied their own taxes and raised their own retainers. Those committed against Huang Chao were mostly the troops of the Xuanhai jiedushi Qin Yan, the various Henan circuits, the Zhongwu and Wuning armies, the forces of the Huainan, Zhexi and Lingnan circuits, and troops summoned westward from Hedong and Guanzhong. These forces were not under one another's command: they would assemble on an imperial summons and then drift back to their own circuits as the orders changed, and what coordination existed between them was maintained only by the rescripts and by the eunuch monitors. The rebel side was the host Huang Chao led, which the court's edicts called the grass bandits: it flew yellow banners and styled itself the formation that dashes at heaven. After taking Guangzhou in 877 he gave up the revenue and the population of Lingnan and marched out with his men to the north; in practice this was a mobile mass army made up mainly of salt smugglers and jobless peasants, with a few tens of thousands of horsemen attached. Inside the rebel army there was a small staff core: Shang Rang as strategist, with Zhang Xilie, Ge Congzhou and others as generals, the host broken into ying and dui, living off the country as it moved, building no entrenched camps and no foundries, taking a walled city when it could be taken and going round it when it could not. After the flight to Jiannan, the escorting central army was set up to guard the imperial party, while the eastern circuits went on fighting their own private wars. At the level of command the two sides were not symmetrical at all: one was a loose federation sending out troops on four sides, the other a single will riding on backward equipment.
people: 核心人物是黃巢。他起自曹州濟陰的鹽梟，乾符二年（875）與王仙芝同起於曹、濮，乾符三年（876）兩軍合於河南，兵眾合為一部。乾符四年（877）王仙芝在江淮受挫，退保狼虎山（其地今屬何處，諸說不一），朝廷赦其罪、授官招安，誘使他離開黃巢；王仙芝既受招安又不肯束手，乾符五年（878）七月在武昌一帶被自己手下的判官與隨行內監合謀殺死。此事後來成為宦官干政、朝廷自壞其手的著名案例，也讓黃巢成為叛軍唯一不可替代的核心。黃巢帳下有尚讓任謀主，葛從周等為大將；官軍方面，兗海節度使秦彥是前期在汝州一線逼退王仙芝的主將，揚州節度使高驃坐擁江淮精兵卻稱病不出，屢為黃巢所輕，終致江淮兵柄旁落；嶺南節度使劉崇謨在廣州陷落時出奔；杭州刺史董彥升在城破時死於任上，浙西一路因此震動。潼關與洛陽的守將姓名各書記載不一，只可知關城守將在數日之內全軍覆沒，隨後僖宗出奔劍南成都。朱溫自嶺北起就在黃巢麾下，是日後反噬舊主的關鍵人物；李克用其時尚未參戰，直到883年才自河東出師追巢。
peopleEn: The central figure is Huang Chao himself. He came from Caozhou as a salt smuggler, rose with Wang Xianzhi in Cao and Puyou at the end of the Qianfu second year (875), and in the third year (876) the two hosts joined in Henan and were merged into one. In the fourth year (877) Wang Xianzhi was checked in the Jianghuai and fell back to Langhushan, whose modern identification is a matter of several competing accounts; the court pardoned him and offered him office, hoping to lure him away from Huang Chao. Having both accepted the pardon and refused to lay himself down, he was murdered in the Wuchang area in the seventh month of the fifth year (878) by a conspiracy between his own pan judge and the eunuch who accompanied him. The affair later became a celebrated case of eunuch interference and of the court ruining its own hands, and it left Huang Chao as the one irreplaceable core of the rebels. Under Huang Chao, Shang Rang served as strategist, with Ge Congzhou and others as generals. On the government side, Qin Yan, jiedushi of Xuanhai, was the commander who had driven Wang Xianzhi back from the line of Ruzhou in the earlier phase; Yangzhou jiedushi Gao Pian sat on the picked troops of the Jianghuai and yet claimed illness and never moved, and was repeatedly held in contempt by Huang Chao, until the military power of the Jianghuai slipped out of Tang hands; the Lingnan jiedushi Liu Chongmo fled when Guangzhou fell; and the Hangzhou governor Dong Yansheng was killed at his post when the city was taken, which shook the whole Zhexi circuit. The names of the defenders of Tong Pass and of Luoyang differ from book to book; all that can be said is that the garrison of the pass was wiped out within a few days, and the emperor fled to Chengdu in Jiannan immediately afterwards. Zhu Wen had been with Huang Chao's host since the north of Lingnan and was the man who would one day turn on his old master; Li Keyong took no part in this war at all and only marched out of Hedong to hunt Huang Chao in 883.
kits: 卡面這柄埃及月牙劍並沒有出現在唐末的戰場上。它是古埃及自早王朝以來就用於近身格殺的青銅弧刃單刃劍：刃口開在凸面，砍進人身或盾牌之後不必回抽拔出，比直刃劍更早成熟，約在公元前1550年前後的新王國時期逐漸讓位給直背長刃；其「砍下去不用拔」的邏輯，本質是弧刃加大劈砍動能，同時減少拔刀時的摩擦。唐軍在875至883年的實際裝備另是一套體系：近身以橫刀為主，環首直身，單刃或雙刃，即漢晉環首刀一系的直刃化；軍中長刀另有陌刀與步槊，劍在唐已是禮器與儀仗之物，寶劍儀刀多見於朝會與儀衛，並非野戰主兵。叛軍是流民與鹽梟起家，兵器多為市集打造的朴刀、砍刀、扁擔改製的長槍、木盾與皮兜鍪，弩機與竹箭則大量取自州縣武庫。攻城方面雙方共有雲梯、飛梯、撞車與破城槌，另有盛油燃火的攻城器與「飛火」；守城以弩為主，唐軍有蹶張弩與臂弩，據《通典》兵法卷所載，弩分數等、長短各異，張弦以足或以機。護具方面，明光鎧、頭盔與護項沿用漢魏舊制而日趨簡化，皮甲與藤牌混用；沙陀騎兵則用蕃刀，即帶弧度的單刃馬刀，正是與月牙劍同一技術路線的後身——從埃及弧刃，經亞述與薩珊一路西來，於唐代以「蕃刀」之名入華，再往下演成明清的環首彎刀與倭刀。交通靠馬與驢騾，軍糧多取自沿途州縣與運河轉運，江淮一段曾因糧道被斷而屢屢停滯。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card did not appear on any battlefield of the late Tang. It was a bronze single-edged sword of crescent curvature used in Egypt for close killing from the Old Kingdom onward: the edge lay on the convex side, and once it had been driven into a body or a shield it did not have to be pulled back out, so it matured earlier than the straight-edged sword, and around 1550 BC, in the New Kingdom, it was gradually displaced by straight-backed long blades. The logic of not withdrawing after the cut is simply that a curved edge adds momentum to the blow and reduces the friction of drawing the blade out again. The actual equipment of the Tang armies between 875 and 883 belonged to a different system altogether. At close quarters the hengdao, a straight-bodied ring-pommel sword of single or double edge, was standard, the straightened descendant of the ring-pommel knives of the Han and Jin; the army had its own long blades in the modao and the ceremonial glaive, while the sword itself had become a ritual object and an item of court display, and treasured dao and ceremonial blades were seen at audiences and in the guard of honour rather than in the line of battle. The rebels came out of vagrants and salt smugglers: their weapons were mostly plain-shop choppers, broad chopping knives, long spears improvised from carrying poles, wooden shields and leather caps, while crossbow frames and bamboo bolts were taken in bulk from the arsenals of the prefectures and counties. For siege both sides had scaling ladders, flying ladders, battering rams and picks, along with oil-filled fire-throwing devices and the so-called flying fire; for defence the crossbow was the main arm, the Tang having the pedal-drawn crossbow and the arm-mounted crossbow, and the bingfa chapter of the Tongdian records that crossbows came in several grades and lengths, strung by foot or by mechanism. Protection was the Mingguang brigandine, helmets and neck guards carried over from Han and Wei but steadily simplified, with leather armour and rattan shields used alongside; the Shatuo horsemen used the fantao, the single-edged curved sabre, which is precisely the later descendant of the same line of technique as the khopesh: from the Egyptian crescent blade, westward carried by Assyria and the Sasanians, entering China in the Tang under the name of the foreign sabre, and running on downwards into the ring-pommel curved swords and the wotou of the Ming and Qing. Movement was by horse, donkey and mule; the grain of the army was taken mostly from the prefectures and counties along the route and from the canal, and in the Jianghuai stretch the food line was cut more than once, so the columns stalled again and again.
tactics: 這場轉戰的戰術本質是一場超長距離的機動作戰。黃巢放棄廣州之後，沒有沿江佈防，而是集中兵力沿海岸與運河水系北進：自嶺北取道江南，連下杭州、越州、潤州、揚州，渡江而後沿淮水與汴泗故道直指中原，攻克亳、泗、楚諸州，再乘勝進逼汴州與洛陽。走法上是典型的避實擊虛：城守嚴整、府庫充實的大城，能攻則攻、不能攻則捨；遇到成建制的方鎮軍則避開主力另尋小股，飢疲與補給的壓力被轉嫁給沿線州縣。叛軍不作深營固守，也不建立後方基地，糧秣靠掠取與就地徵發，攻一城即取一城之糧，因此能以遠低於其聲勢的人數維持長距離機動作戰，這也是它能連續推進的原因。官軍這一邊則陷入典型的中晚唐協同失敗：各道節度使各守本境，詔書到處而兵不歸一處，虛報戰功、隱匿實情，援軍常在百里之外徘徊；城守方倚城牆與弩，以強弩壓制叛軍的攻城隊形，再以輕騎或小股兵力出城擾其糧道，然後退回城中。潼關一線的攻防最為關鍵：關隘夾在山水之間，通道狹窄，官軍倚險用弩、拒叛軍於關外，結果在關門被突破之後，兩京之間再無可以倚恃的屏障，潰兵與器械散落一路，汴州與洛陽相繼淪陷。追擊與反追擊的技藝此時尚未成形，真正成熟的追擊戰要到883年河東沙陀騎兵出現才開始：沙陀騎兵以蕃刀砍劈為主，配長槊，縱騎衝突，是對流寇式轉戰最有效的破解辦法。
tacticsEn: The tactical essence of this campaign was a movement operation of extraordinary length. After giving up Guangzhou, Huang Chao did not hold a line along the river but concentrated his force and moved north along the coast and the waterways of the canal system: from the north of Lingnan he took the route through Jiangnan, took Hangzhou, Yuezhou, Runzhou and Yangzhou in turn, crossed the Yangtze, and then followed the Huai and the old Bian-S waterways straight for the Central Plain, taking Bo, Si and Chu, and pressed on to Bianzhou and Luoyang. The method was an evasion of the strong and an attack on the weak: a great walled city with a careful garrison and a full treasury was taken if it could be taken and abandoned if it could not; a formed provincial army was avoided in its main body and smaller detachments hunted instead, and hunger and the pressure of supply were passed on to the prefectures along the route. The rebels did not dig in with deep entrenched camps and built no base behind them; their grain was taken by plunder and levied on the spot, and taking a city meant taking that city's grain, which is how they could keep a long movement going with far fewer men than their numbers suggested. The government side suffered the classic failure of coordination of the middle and late Tang: each circuit defended its own ground, the rescripts travelled everywhere and the troops came to no single place, victories were reported that had not been won and the truth of the situation was concealed, and relief forces often hovered a hundred li away; the defenders relied on the wall and the crossbow, held the rebels' siege formations down with strong crossbow fire, and sent light horse or small detachments out of the gate to harry the enemy supply line before falling back inside. The fighting at Tong Pass was the most critical of all: the pass lay between mountain and water with a narrow defile, the defenders used the ground and their crossbows to hold the rebels outside the gate, and once the gate was forced there was no barrier left between the two capitals. The broken troops and abandoned engines littered the road, and Bianzhou and Luoyang fell in turn. The art of pursuit and of counter-pursuit was not yet formed; the mature pursuit war only began in 883 with the arrival of the Shatuo cavalry from Hedong, which fought with the curved foreign sabre and the long spear, charging on horseback, and which was the most effective answer to the way the rebels moved.
data: 可核對的數字分五類，而且都帶著明顯的不確定。第一類是年代：卡片所繫的877年即唐乾符四年，是黃巢放棄廣州、決定轉戰中原的年份；實際推進貫穿乾符四年全年至乾符五年（878）初夏，其攻洛陽、入長安的關鍵戰鬥落在878年，隨後僖宗出奔劍南，黃巢建國號大齊、年號金統，佔據京師約兩年，883年為河東軍所破，884年死於泰山狼虎谷一帶。第二類是編制與制度數字：唐軍步軍以十人為火，五火為隊，五隊為旅，五旅為師，五師為軍，一軍之制為六千二百五十人；各鎮節度使所募部曲的數目史無明文。《唐律疏議》把甲、胄、弩、矛、盾列為禁兵器，民間私蓄受罰，故弩與甲的來源受限，軍械集於官府。第三類是傳世常見而互相矛盾的兵力數：叛軍在攻廣州時的眾數，諸書有十餘萬、數十萬乃至六十萬等不同記載，多數學者認為實際作戰兵力在數萬至十餘萬之間，其中多為裹挾的農民；官軍方面因節度使各自為戰，總數無從核實，只留下各書互異的斬首與俘獲戰報，沒有可信的總傷亡數字。第四類是里程：廣州至杭州直線約一千三百公里，杭州至長安直線亦約一千三百公里，汴州至洛陽約四百公里，這條越嶺、渡江、穿淮、抵兩京的路線長度，本身即是這場戰爭最大的戰術變數；傳統驛道一日約一百至一百五十里，全線行軍以月計。第五類是氣候與季節：江南梅雨與江北寒潮交替，冬季渡江與春季進軍都直接影響糧秣與士氣，諸書屢以久雨與霜寒記軍隊停滯。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into five classes, each with an obvious measure of uncertainty. The first is chronology. The year 877 on the card is the Qianfu fourth year of the Tang, the year in which Huang Chao gave up Guangzhou and resolved to turn his host towards the Central Plain. The movement itself ran through the whole of the fourth year into the early summer of the fifth year (878); the decisive fighting for Luoyang and for Chang'an falls in 878, the flight of the emperor to Jiannan follows, Huang Chao founds the state of Daqi with the era name Jintong, and he holds the capital for roughly two years, until he is broken by the Hedong army in 883 and dies in the neighbourhood of Langhu Valley on Mount Tai in 884. The second class is establishment and institutional figures. Tang infantry were organised ten men to a huo, five huo to a dui, five dui to a lü, five lü to a shi and five shi to a jun, which gives a regulation strength of 6,250 men for one jun; the numbers of retainers raised by the individual jiedushi are nowhere recorded. The Tanglü Shiyi lists armour, helmets, crossbows, spears and shields as prohibited weapons, and private possession of them was punished, so the supply of crossbows and armour was restricted and the ordnance was held by the government. The third class is the strength figures that are constantly quoted and constantly contradict one another. For the numbers of Huang Chao's host at the taking of Guangzhou the books give ten-odd thousand, several tens of thousands and even six hundred thousand; most scholars would put the actual field strength somewhere between several tens of thousands and a hundred-odd thousand, most of them peasants swept along. On the government side no total can be checked at all, because each circuit fought its own war, and only the various captures and severed heads reported in the books survive, with no dependable figure for overall losses. The fourth class is distance. Guangzhou to Hangzhou is about 1,300 kilometres as the crow flies, Hangzhou to Chang'an about the same, and Bianzhou to Luoyang about 400. The sheer length of that route, over the ranges, across the river, through the Huai and on to the two capitals, is in itself the greatest tactical variable in the war. The old courier stations allowed about 100 to 150 li a day, so the whole march was counted in months. The fifth class is season and weather. The plum rains of Jiangnan and the cold waves north of the Yangtze alternate, and both a winter crossing and a spring advance bear directly on the grain supply and on the morale of the troops, and the books repeatedly record the columns standing still under long rain and hard frost.
cause: 打起來的根子有四層。第一層是唐廷的財政與體制：安史之亂後兩稅法、鹽鐵專賣與進奉逼迫，漕運阻塞，鹽價騰貴，私鹽販成了成千上萬人的生業；王仙芝、黃巢都是曹州一帶的鹽梟，兩人起兵時打的旗號就是販私鹽，這是唐末亂兵的共同出身，也是彼此能合流的前提。第二層是災荒與流亡：關中、河南、江淮連年水旱，饑民入山為盜，過境州縣不能賑恤，於是亂民與亂兵合流。第三層是朝廷的招安分化：對王仙芝的赦免授官，既為了分化，也是出於無力；它犧牲了起義者內部的統一指揮，把唯一能團結數十萬人的首領推到死路，逼出更激烈的一條路。第四層是黃巢在嶺南的處境：攻下廣州之後，嶺南財賦有限，軍眾日增而糧秣無著，黃巢索求巨額金帛不得，遂放棄廣州北還——一次純粹的後勤與政治轉向，卻把整個唐廷推到了生死線上。而唐廷此刻的應手仍然疲弱：各節度使擁兵自重，中央無力統籌，宦官監軍牽制將領，王仙芝之死即是明證；於是875年以來屢屢平而不定的亂局，在877年之後變成了一場直搗兩京的長距離進攻。
causeEn: There are four layers behind the outbreak. The first is the finances and the structure of the Tang court. After the An Lushan rebellion, the two-tax system, the state monopolies on salt and iron and the tribute levies weighed down on the provinces, the grain transport by canal was choked, the price of salt rose steeply, and smuggling salt had become the livelihood of thousands upon thousands. Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao were both salt smugglers of the Caozhou region, and the banner they raised when they rose was the smuggling of salt; that was the common origin of the late Tang rebels, and it was also what allowed the two of them to join. The second layer is famine and displacement. Across Guanzhong, Henan and the Jianghuai there were years of flood and drought in succession, starving people took to the hills as bandits, and the prefectures on the road could not relieve them, so the displaced and the bandits merged. The third layer is the policy of pardon and division pursued by the court. The pardon and the offer of office to Wang Xianzhi were meant both to split the rebels and to express the court's own helplessness; they sacrificed the unity of command inside the uprising, pushed the one leader who could hold several hundred thousand men onto a dead end, and forced a more violent road in consequence. The fourth layer is the position Huang Chao found himself in at Lingnan. After taking Guangzhou he found the wealth of Lingnan limited, his host growing daily and no grain to feed it, and when the large sums of silk and treasure he demanded were not forthcoming he gave up Guangzhou and marched north. A turn driven purely by supply and by politics in this way pushed the whole Tang court onto the line of life and death. And the court's answering hand was still weak: the jiedushi held their troops for themselves, the centre could not coordinate, eunuch monitors held the generals in leash, and the murder of Wang Xianzhi is the plain proof of it. The disorder that had been raised and half-suppressed since 875 thus turned, after 877, into a long-distance attack aimed straight at the two capitals.
impact: 這場戰爭把唐朝的元氣一次抽空，也把晚唐的結構問題全部暴露在光下。第一，中央威信崩解。僖宗出奔劍南，長安兩度淪陷，禁軍宿衛盡散，朝廷自此只能靠藩鎮和宦官維持局面，皇權的合法性要靠外藩的刀兵來證明。第二，藩鎮化加速。追巢的各道節度使因軍功而擴兵，因軍費而截留賦稅，因賞罰而部曲私有化，河東、魏博、盧龍、忠武一類藩鎮在平亂中坐大，晚唐到五代的三藩鎮格局由此成形。第三，北方外族勢力入主。沙陀李克用自河東追巢入關，此後長期以「助唐平亂」的名義駐兵河東、河中，成為唐末最重要的一支外來軍事力量。第四，江南受創而地位上升，兩浙與江南道在亂後因相對安寧而成為藩鎮財源重地，孕育出吳越與南唐那樣的割據政權。第五，戰術層面的示範：黃巢式的流動戰，不據城、不守地、不修壘，專打對方防禦的空隙，成為晚唐五代亂軍的標準樣板，直到沙陀騎兵與藩鎮鎮兵把它壓制住。戰役也把唐代軍備的落後攤在陽光下：禁兵器的律令、募兵之制、節度使自募部曲的體制，使唐廷在面對一支以民間打造武器的流動軍時幾乎無從調度。史家常以黃巢之亂為唐朝崩解的起點，不是因為它推翻了唐，而是因為它把唐廷能用的資源全部耗盡了。
impactEn: This war drained the Tang of its strength in one stroke and exposed every structural weakness of the late Tang to the light. First, the authority of the centre collapsed. Xizong fled to Jiannan, Chang'an fell twice, the palace guards were scattered, and from then on the court could keep itself in being only by means of the regional governors and the eunuchs; the legitimacy of imperial power now had to be demonstrated by the swords of the outer armies. Second, the process of military particularisation accelerated. The jiedushi who chased Huang Chao enlarged their forces on the strength of campaign credits, withheld revenues to pay for them, and turned their retainers into private property through the power of reward and punishment; the regional commands of Hedong, of Weibo, of Lulong and of Zhongwu grew fat out of the suppression, and the three-commandery pattern of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties took shape from it. Third, a northern non-Han military power entered China proper. The Shatuo Li Keyong pursued Huang Chao from Hedong into the passes, and thereafter kept troops stationed in Hedong and Hezhong for long years under the name of helping the Tang put down the rebels, becoming the most important foreign military force of the late Tang. Fourth, the Jiangnan was damaged but rose in standing: after the fighting, the Zhexi and Jiangnan circuits, relatively peaceful, became the main sources of revenue for the regional governors and produced the breakaway regimes of Wuyue and Southern Tang. Fifth, the campaign gave a tactical demonstration. The mobile war of the Huang Chao type, which held no city, kept no ground, built no entrenchments and struck only where the defence was thin, became the standard pattern for the rebel armies of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties, and it was not put down until the Shatuo cavalry and the provincial levies arrived to counter it. The war also laid the backwardness of Tang military finance in the open: the statutes forbidding private weapons, the recruitment system, and the practice by which each jiedushi raised his own retainers left the court with almost no means of directing a mobile army whose weapons were forged in the markets. Historians commonly take the Huang Chao rising as the beginning of the dissolution of the Tang, not because it overthrew the Tang, but because it used up every resource the court still had.
result: 結果要分兩層看。就877年這場轉戰本身而言，黃巢是完勝的：他放棄廣州，以一次長距離的連續機動，吃掉了江淮與河南之間的所有空隙，攻破杭州、越州、潤州、揚州，渡江後連取亳、泗、楚諸州，進逼汴州，最終在乾符五年（878）拔洛陽、入長安，僖宗出奔成都，朝廷在形式上覆亡，黃巢即位建大齊、年號金統。就戰役的技術層面而言，進攻方有兩個決定性的優勢，也有兩個致命弱點：優勢是速度，線性推進、不作深營，使唐軍各鎮總是慢一步；弱點同樣明顯，沒有後方、沒有根據地、沒有可持續的稅源，糧秣只能靠沿途取給，一旦深入而州縣不從或道路被斷，士氣與軍紀立刻崩解，黃巢大軍北潰時的混亂即出於此。戰局的反轉在883年：河東沙陀軍追至河南，連敗叛軍於汴、洛之間，進逼京師，黃巢退保泰山狼虎谷，884年兵敗而死；傳世記載謂尚讓等在山東另立其弟黃邈為帝，年號黃統，餘部後來有的受招安成為官軍所用的部曲，有的流為盜匪，與同期其他藩鎮的亂軍混成五代亂世的底色。歷史的評價因此是兩句話並列：黃巢轉戰中原之戰，在戰術上是流寇式機動作戰的頂點，在戰略上是唐朝中央權威的終點；它結束了節度使剿亂、各自為政的舊式平亂模式，把亂軍推到兩京門下，也把後來數十年藩鎮混戰的劇本提前寫好。
resultEn: The outcome has to be read on two levels. As far as the campaign of 877 itself is concerned, Huang Chao won it completely. He gave up Guangzhou and, in a single long sequence of movements, took in every gap between the Jianghuai and Henan: he carried Hangzhou, Yuezhou, Runzhou and Yangzhou, crossed the Yangtze and took Bo, Si and Chu in turn, pressed on to Bianzhou, and in the fifth year of Qianfu (878) took Luoyang and entered Chang'an. The emperor fled to Chengdu, the court was destroyed in form, and Huang Chao mounted the throne as founder of Daqi with the era name Jintong. On the technical level the attacker had two decisive advantages and two fatal weaknesses. The advantages were speed: a linear advance with no deep entrenched camps meant that the separate Tang circuits were always one step behind. The weaknesses were just as plain: there was no rear, no base area and no sustainable source of revenue, grain could only be taken from the country along the route, and once the host had gone deep and the prefectures would not follow or the road was cut, morale and discipline collapsed at once, which is exactly what the confusion of the northern flight shows. The reversal came in 883, when the Hedong Shatuo army overtook the rebels in Henan and beat them repeatedly between Bian and Luo, pressing on to the capital; Huang Chao withdrew to Langhu Valley on Mount Tai and was killed in 884. The transmitted account has it that Shang Rang and the others set up his brother Huang Miao as emperor in Shandong under the era name Huangtong, and that the survivors were in part taken into the government's service as troops and in part turned into bandit bands, mingling with the rebel armies of the other circuits to form the base of the disorder of the Five Dynasties. The historical judgement therefore takes the form of two sentences set side by side. In tactics the campaign of Huang Chao's march into the Central Plain was the summit of the mobile war of the wandering armies; in strategy it was the end of the central authority of the Tang. It closed the old pattern in which the jiedushi suppressed the trouble each on their own, it carried the rebels to the gates of the two capitals, and it wrote out in advance the scenario of the factional wars among the regional commands that were to run for decades to come.
